label: exploratory: labels by Claude (an LLM, not a person) from sheets without the checker's flags, by the protocol committed before the explanations existed

numbers_detail.note: the text's 'thirty percent' (0.3 in the model)

explanations_detail.note: budget called not the bottleneck because $2 is unspent, but $2 buys no trip: +$4 of budget gives 890 (10 rickshaw, 13 ox cart); without it, unbounded (enumerated)

Says the leftover amounts mean the store isn't at full capacity and the whole-number requirement limits the result most. Capital is the limit: the $50 left is less than one chair's $150 (with $20,150 of capital the optimum is 134 chairs, $10,050); dropping integrality gains only $25 (133.33 chairs, $10,000), dropping the capital limit gives $20,700 (brute force). Capital has slack only because of integrality; it binds in the LP relaxation.

Says the budget ($400 slack) is not what holds the result back. It is a limit: $400 can't buy another magazine ad ($1000), $600 more would add 10,000 viewers (49 magazine ads), and with no budget the maximum is unbounded. MIP slack read as 'not limiting' (checked by enumeration).
hardware (1 h spare) called not what limits production, but it caps foldables: +6 h gives $16,600 (8 foldable, 42 regular); without it $25,000 (enumerated)
first sentence states a wrong plan ('devote all 120 acres'; land has 70 acres of slack) before retracting it ('... no, plant 50 acres')

Integer effect: says the drying machine (20 s left) is not what limits the result, but it is: 10 more seconds allow 37 regular + 40 premium = 194 people (> 193), and without the drying limit the optimum is 202 (checked by enumeration).
25% salmon cap (0.25 slack) called not holding the plan back, but it is: +0.75 gives 102 g (3 salmon, 6 bison); without it 82 g (enumerated); protein part is right

Integer effect: says the 3-to-1 medium/specialty rule (2 bags to spare) isn't what holds the total down, but it is what stops a 13th specialty bag (that needs 39 medium, 52 bags in all); relaxed by 2 the total is 415, dropped it is 600 (checked by enumeration).

Says the plan is not held back by the demand requirement. It is what sets the answer: 12 large lines make only 6000 < 6300 sets, and with no demand requirement the minimum is 0 lines. MIP slack read as 'not limiting' (checked by enumeration).
says the binding XYZ minimum 'holds the count down'; a minimum holds the count up: without it the fewest is 13, and XYZ >= 4 allows 10 + 4 = 14
Says the solver reports no shadow prices because no constraint is binding. There are none because it is a MIP; an LP reports them, zero for non-binding constraints.

Says the twice-as-much-vanilla rule isn't what limits the result because it has room to spare (slack 2). It does limit: chocolate gives 5 g of protein per g of sugar against vanilla's 2.6, and the rule blocks 28 chocolate + 55 vanilla (497 g of sugar, 1,550 g of protein); without the rule the optimum is 2,500 g (brute force). Slack only at the integer optimum; it binds in the LP relaxation.

Integer effect: says the 750-unit rule (10 units spare) is not limiting, but it is what forces 10 cargo trips (9 carry 720 < 750); without it the optimum is 250 (2 cargo trips), and at 720 units it is 390 (checked by enumeration).

calls the expert share (0.9 shifts spare) closest to its limit by comparing shifts with square meters; land is closer: 20 m2 is 0.4% of 5,000 and under one shift, so dropping any shift breaks it, while 6 experts of 60 still meet 10%

Says the 30% coffee rule (0.1 to spare) doesn't restrict the result. It does: without it, 0 coffees and 1 cappuccino (4 units of water) meet every other rule, against 10 (brute force); it is the rule that forces a coffee into the mix. Slack only at the integer optimum; it binds in the LP relaxation.

Says the internal-driver share rule (slack 0.8) is not what limits the plan. It is what forces 4 internal drivers: without it, 15 external drivers give pollution 75 instead of 108. MIP slack read as 'not limiting' (checked by enumeration).

goods requirement (15 spare) called not the main constraint, but it sets the helicopter count: loosening by 5 gives 310 min (5 airplanes, 16 helicopters); without it 210 min (enumerated); helicopter-rule part is right
Says the small >= 3x large rule (slack 2) does not limit the plan. It does: without it, 14 large trailers (84 cars) beat 18 trailers. MIP slack read as 'not limiting' (checked by enumeration).

Reads the binding 100-unit minimum as a cap: says adding more units would need a requirement change. A >= minimum never stops adding units (electricity does, as the next sentence says); the binding minimum holds the maximum down by forcing elevators in place of escalators (without it: 82 escalators + 10 elevators, 206,800).
vitamin and fiber targets called not what holds the plan in place, but the vitamin target does: loosening by 2 gives 48 (14 fruit, 6 veg); without it 42 (12, 6) (enumerated); fiber alone is right

Says the bus-to-gondola ratio (slack 2) isn't what holds the plan back. It is: without it, 18 gondolas and 28 buses (46 in all) meet the 500-per-minute target and the 40% gondola share rule, against 79 (brute force); it binds in the LP relaxation and keeps gondolas, which carry 4 times as many people, to 7. (Loosening it by 2 changes nothing; the share-rule half of the sentence is true.)
Says the milk share stays 0.8 below the 10% cap, but 0.8 is the cap constraint's slack in cups (1 cup of milk vs 10% of 18 = 1.8 cups); the share itself is 1/18 = 5.6%, 4.4 points below 10%.
